results.title: Asymmetric Information and R&D Disclosure: Evidence from ...
results.content: Difference-in-differences regressions around brokerage house mergers and closures, which increase information asymmetry through reductions in analyst coverage, indicate a quick and sustained increase in scientific publications from treated firms relative to the number of publications from control firms. Although we focus on scientific publications, we acknowledge that firms may also choose alternative R&D disclosure strategies in response to adverse shocks to information asymmetry. Third, instead of interpreting scientific publications as a measure for R&D investment, we interpret the relation between publication rates and coverage as evidence that firms change their level of scientific disclosure in response to changes in the number of analysts following them. The point estimate in this column is 0.119, indicating that an increase in asymmetric information because of coverage shocks causes the firm to increase its scientific publications by approximately 12.6% (=𝑒0.119−1) relative to the number of publications of firms with no decrease in analyst coverage.
